rows: Look for exceptions; extreme statements are usually false
Rephrase the question stem as a simple True/False test
Excessively long text or complex calculations
Skip on first pass; return only after solving easy items

items: Always circle or highlight absolute qualifiers like 'Always', 'Never', and 'Only' before picking an option.
Double-check option numbers when filling answer sheets, especially after skipping difficult questions.
Beware of options that look familiar from formulas but miss basic unit conversions.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Exam traps are engineered to exploit candidate speed, overconfidence, and fatigue under pressure.
Negative stems containing terms like 'NOT', 'INCORRECT', or 'EXCEPT' cause maximum unforced errors.
Partial truth options present correct premises with subtly flawed conclusions to mislead hasty readers.
Time-sink questions are strategically positioned to disrupt overall paper pacing and time management.
